correctness.rationale: Euclidean primitive parametrization bijects m>n coprime opposite parity to odd coprime 0<u=m-n<v=m+n, with hypotenuse (u²+v²)/2 and odd leg uv. Because gcd(u,v)=1, k-power-freeness of uv is equivalent to that of u and v. The sector 0<u<v, u²+v²<=2X has area pi X/4; both odd imposes factor 1/4; at p>2 admissibility is lambda_(p,k)=1-p^-2-2*p^-k*(1-p^-1)=(1-p^-2)*(1-2/(p^(k-1)*(p+1))). For fixed z the CRT sieve gives density, while uniform large-prime tails O_k(X/z+sqrt(X)log X) justify z->infty after X->infty, proving T_k(X)=X/(2pi)*prod_{p>2}(1-2/(p^(k-1)(p+1)))+o_k(X). Independent Euclid-vs-odd-factor enumeration agrees for all 9 (X,k) pairs X=50,500,10000 and k=2,3,4; product through 200000 gives P2 approximately .70752146, matching reported normalization. Infinite asymptotic follows only from the analytic sieve, not experiments.

value.rationale: Power-free arithmetic properties of the unique odd leg are natural: a primitive triangle always has its even leg divisible by 4, so its squarefreeness is impossible. The theorem identifies the exact positive proportion (including squarefree P2~.70752) among all primitive triangles ordered by hypotenuse and extends coherently to each fixed k, a meaningful quantitative invariant not a contrived finite slice.
